segments.text: Vortex, level six.
The goal is the vortex7 password, from /vortex/vortex6: a setuid vortex7 binary with no published source.
The binary copies itself so I can read it, and I measure it with md5.
The first question is what the program does when run plain, and it hangs: a detached run under timeout produces a zero-byte output file, so the process never returns.

The disassembly shows why: restart takes the argument, drops privileges with setreuid, and re-execs it, and main passes argv zero, not argv one, so running the binary re-execs itself forever, an infinite exec loop.
The same restart is the way out: point argv zero at /bin/sh instead, and the setuid binary drops us into a shell as vortex7.
The stack is not executable, and there is a format-string hole in printf argv three, but with the stack read-only the restart is the whole exploit.
I log in as vortex6.
I make /tmp/l6rec and move in.
The hang test first: a detached run under timeout three, then four seconds, and the output file reads zero bytes, the infinite exec loop confirmed.
I copy the binary and read it with md5.
objdump shows restart: setreuid of the effective id twice, then execlp of the argument.
objdump shows main: the argv zero test, the restart call, printf of argv three, and an exit with the status of the level number.
readelf shows GNU_STACK read-write only, no shellcode.
And the password file is ten bytes, mode four hundred.
I open vim and write the runner: it execs the binary with argv zero pointed at /bin/sh.
First the payload lists: /bin/sh as the program name, and a short PATH and TERM as the environment, both null-terminated.
Then the library handle, the two C arrays for the argument and environment lists, and the exec call.
The file is 12 lines, 440 bytes.

The run pipes id and a read of the password file into the runner: execve of /vortex/vortex6 with argv zero of /bin/sh, the setuid binary drops us into a shell as vortex7, and the piped commands run inside it.
I log out of vortex6.
Then I log in as vortex7 with the password the shell read.
id confirms uid five thousand seven, vortex7.
And the password file reads back the same password.
The level is solved.
I log out.
